tasks.short: Check clocked hours, overtime and allowances against rosters before they go into AFAS for the month.

today.trigger: Weekly hours exports from the three sites and the month-end payroll deadline.
steps: Pull the clocking or hours export per site into Excel
Compare it line by line with shift rosters and approved overtime mails from team leads
Check shift and overtime allowances against the two CAOs
Chase site managers by Outlook or Teams about missing or odd hours
Key the corrected hours and allowance lines into AFAS Profit
drudgery: Matching roster lines to clock lines by hand
today.time_sinks: Chasing team leads about missed clock-ins and unapproved overtime, mostly in the last week before close.

lenses.faster: A rule script matches hours to rosters, applies CAO allowance rules and posts clean lines to AFAS. The specialist only works the exception list, which takes about 40% of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: Each nightly hours export starts the match. Clean lines post to AFAS on their own, and lines outside the rules go to a queue that the specialist or team lead approves.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: hours are checked daily instead of at month end, so team leads fix a missed clock-in the next day. Demand would grow because site managers want the same check for their own planning.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss the line-by-line Excel match. The specialist wants more time on fixing why one site keeps producing the same errors.
lenses.options: Little value in several drafts here: a line either passes the rules or it does not.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from matching to tuning the allowance rules per CAO and agreeing approval rules with site managers. The specialist gains the right to set which deviations block posting.
reach: Take over the per-site hours sign-off that HR Administrators chase today; this needs the roster logic of each warehouse

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether an unusual overtime pattern is a real rush, a roster mistake or misuse, and talking that through with the team lead.
tasks.pattern_why: Matching hours to rosters and applying CAO allowance rules can be written down in full, so no model is needed to decide.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly hours export lands in the payroll SharePoint folder.
steps: Script loads hours, rosters and approved overtime
Script applies CAO allowance and overtime rules per site
Clean lines post to AFAS Profit as pending mutations
Exceptions are listed with reason codes
Team lead or specialist approves or corrects each exception
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist or the team lead approves every exception line before it posts.
in_practice.logs_to: An exception log in SharePoint showing who approved what, kept with the month's payroll file.

evidence.claim: Pay calculation and its checks stay deterministic and rules-based in production payroll tools.
In AFAS Profit, payroll lines approve automatically once a person approves the declaration: a rule after a human gate.

risks: One error in a CAO allowance rule pays hundreds of people wrong at once
The works council may see automatic hours checks as monitoring of staff (WOR 27)
Site hours exports differ in format and can break the script
research_questions: How many hour lines per month fall outside the rules today, per site?
Can the hours export reach AFAS Profit through its API without a manual upload?
Does the works council treat a daily hours check as a staff monitoring system that needs its consent?

tasks.short: Enter monthly pay changes, bonuses, deductions and wage garnishments into AFAS and check the gross-to-net result.

today.trigger: Monthly payroll close and mutation mails coming in from HR and managers.
steps: Collect pay changes from mails, forms and Excel lists
Enter allowances, bonuses and deductions as AFAS mutations
Work out garnishments (loonbeslag) and advance repayments by hand
Run the test payroll in AFAS and spot-check gross-to-net
Correct and rerun
drudgery: Typing the same mutation types into AFAS every month
today.time_sinks: Collecting scattered mutation requests and redoing entries after a late change.

lenses.faster: AFAS keeps doing the calculation. A script turns structured mutation lists into AFAS imports and recalculates the protected income limit (beslagvrije voet), so the specialist only checks totals and exceptions, cutting about 45% of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A closed mutation list starts the import and AFAS runs the test payroll. The specialist approves the run before payment.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: a test payroll runs every week, not once a month, so late changes stop causing correction runs. Demand would grow because managers no longer wait a month for a change.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss retyping mutations. The specialist wants more time on garnishment cases and on staff in money trouble.
lenses.options: Scenario runs matter when the company changes a CAO allowance or bonus scheme: they show the cost and net effect of two or three variants before the decision.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the import templates and the test that a run is first-time-right, with the right to stop a run.
reach: Prepare the payroll journal for the Accountant's month close; this needs the AFAS ledger mapping

tasks.human_edge: Handling garnishment and debt cases with the employee and the bailiff, where both the law and the person's situation matter.
tasks.pattern_why: Gross-to-net and deductions are fixed rules already built into AFAS, and generated pay calculations are not acceptable.

in_practice.trigger: The month's mutation cut-off date passes.
steps: Script checks the mutation list against fixed formats
Mutations import into AFAS Profit
AFAS runs the test payroll
Script compares totals with last month and flags outliers
Specialist approves the run
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves the test payroll before the final run and the payment batch to Rabobank.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS mutation history, plus a run approval note in the payroll SharePoint file.

evidence.claim: Payroll vendors keep pay calculation deterministic and put AI around it.
Workday states that a good guess is not good enough in payroll.

risks: A wrong import template repeats one error across many employees
A wrong automated protected income limit hurts staff who are already in debt
research_questions: What share of monthly mutations already arrive in a structured form?
How many correction runs per year come from late or mistyped mutations?
Does AFAS Profit support bulk import for every mutation type Noordhaven uses?

tasks.short: Keep vacation, special leave and sick leave balances right in AFAS for office and shift staff.

today.trigger: Leave requests, sick reports and year-end balance checks.
steps: Check leave requests and approvals in AFAS
Correct balances by hand for part-timers and shift workers
Register sick reports and recovery dates for absence (verzuim)
Answer staff questions on remaining days
Settle expiring and paid-out leave at year end
drudgery: Recomputing balances after contract hour changes
Answering the same 'how many days do I have left' mails
today.time_sinks: Year-end checks on statutory versus extra leave, and on CAO-specific build-up rules for shift workers.

lenses.faster: Leave build-up and expiry rules for each CAO run as fixed rules in AFAS, with a nightly balance check. Manual corrections and questions drop by about half.
lenses.autonomous: Any change in contract hours or leave registration triggers a recalculation. Only balances that break a rule reach the specialist.
lenses.ambitious: A group served for the first time: shift workers in Tilburg and Venlo see their own balance and expiry dates every week on their phone instead of mailing payroll or asking the team lead. Demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss the year-end hunt for balances. The specialist wants more time explaining leave rights to the people who need it.
lenses.options: Little: the rules decide the balances.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the leave rule set for both CAOs and decides with the HR Business Partner how to handle gaps. The job gets more expert on leave law.
reach: Feed sick-leave dates into the HR Business Partner's Wet verbetering poortwachter file; this needs the poortwachter timeline

tasks.human_edge: Cases where leave and sickness overlap, or where a manager and an employee disagree about which days were approved.
tasks.pattern_why: Leave build-up, expiry and sick-leave registration follow written CAO and legal rules.

in_practice.trigger: A change in contract hours, a leave request or a sick report in AFAS.
steps: Recalculate the balance under the CAO rule
Compare it with the stored balance
Flag differences and expiring days
Tell the employee about upcoming expiry
Specialist resolves the flagged cases
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves corrections to a balance before they change pay or a payout.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS leave history, plus a correction log.

evidence.claim: Leave and absence records already sit in AFAS Profit, and leave balances can be calculated by fixed rules without a model.

risks: Sick-leave data is health data under the AVG, so access must stay narrow
Wrong expiry notices cause disputes with staff
research_questions: How many manual balance corrections were made last year?
Are both CAOs' leave rules already set up in AFAS, or kept in Excel?
Can shift workers reach AFAS self-service on a phone today?

tasks.short: Process resignations, site transfers and tax credit choices into employee pay records in AFAS.

today.trigger: A resignation letter, transfer request or new payroll tax credit (loonheffingskorting) form arrives by mail or from HR.
steps: Read the letter or form and check the notice period
Enter the end date, transfer or tax credit change in AFAS
Work out final pay items such as leave payout
Tell HR, the manager and the pension provider
File the document in the personnel file
drudgery: Retyping data from letters and forms
Checking notice periods per contract by hand
today.time_sinks: Back-and-forth with HR about dates and missing signatures.

lenses.faster: A model reads the letter or form and fills a draft AFAS mutation, with dates and a notice period check. The specialist checks and approves, cutting about 45% of the time.
lenses.autonomous: A mail into the payroll mailbox starts the extraction, and the draft waits in AFAS until it is approved.
lenses.ambitious: A new service for HR Business Partners: leavers get a draft of their final pay statement on the day they resign, for use in exit talks. Demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying from PDFs. The specialist wants more time on complex exits such as settlement agreements.
lenses.options: For exits with a settlement or transition payment, two or three payout scenarios help HR and the employee decide.
lenses.altitude: The specialist moves from typing to approving, and sets which mutation types may be pre-filled. The work gets more expert.
reach: Take over exit mutations from the HR Administrators; this needs the contract and notice rules of both CAOs

tasks.human_edge: Spotting when a resignation hides a dispute or a settlement, and stopping routine processing.
tasks.pattern_why: Letters and forms are messy text, and one model call turns them into a mutation draft that can be checked inside a fixed AFAS flow.

in_practice.trigger: A resignation, transfer or tax credit form arrives in the payroll mailbox.
steps: Model extracts the person, change type, dates and choices
Rules check the notice period and contract
A draft mutation is created in AFAS
Specialist approves or corrects it
Notices go to HR and the manager
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves each mutation before it counts.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS mutation log, with the source document attached.

evidence.claim: A bot that reads the personnel file needs works council consent under WOR 27(1)(k).
AFAS Jonas answers AFAS configuration questions and cites Help Center articles.

risks: Extraction errors on dates lead to wrong final pay
Model processing of personnel documents needs a DPIA and works council consent
research_questions: How many of these mutations arrive per month, and in what formats?
Will the works council accept a model reading personnel documents?
What error rate does extraction reach on a sample of 100 past letters?

tasks.short: Check the test payroll for errors and find out why someone's pay differs from what it should be.

today.trigger: The test payroll run before the monthly close, and complaints after payday.
steps: Compare the test payroll with last month in Excel
Look for large changes per employee
Trace each difference back to hours, mutations or rules
Fix the source and rerun
Explain corrections to employees and managers
drudgery: Building the same comparison sheet every month
today.time_sinks: Explaining each difference: spotting it is quick, finding the cause is slow.

lenses.faster: Fixed checks flag large gross pay changes, stopped pension contributions, leavers paid twice and pay below minimum wage, and a model writes a short explanation for each exception. The specialist still decides each one, cutting time by about half.
lenses.autonomous: Each test run starts the checks, so the exception list with explanations is ready before the specialist begins.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: checks run after every mutation batch instead of once a month, so corrections per run fall. Demand would grow as Finance asks for the same checks on the payroll journal.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss the comparison sheet. The specialist wants more time finding root causes.
lenses.options: Not much: each exception is either right or wrong.
lenses.altitude: The specialist designs the check set and its thresholds and decides when a run may go. First-time-right runs become their measure.
reach: Take over the Controller's payroll journal review; this needs the ledger account mapping

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which changes are expected this month, such as a CAO pay rise or a site reorganisation.
tasks.pattern_why: The checks are deterministic rules, and one model call explains each exception in plain words for review.

steps: Rules compare the run with the prior month and policy limits
Exceptions are listed per employee
Model drafts an explanation of the cause from the mutation history
Specialist accepts, corrects or blocks each item
The approved run goes final
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist decides on each exception and approves the run.
in_practice.logs_to: An exception list with the decision on each item, stored with the run.

evidence.claim: PayCaptain runs these checks in production: unexpected gross pay changes, stopped pension contributions, leavers paid double net, and pay below minimum wage.
Workday's Payroll Agent will flag items outside defined parameters.

risks: An explanation that sounds right but is wrong leads to a wrong approval
Too many false flags, so the list gets ignored
research_questions: How many corrections per run happened in the past 12 months, and what caused them?
Would the four PayCaptain checks have caught them?
Can the specialist check model explanations faster than writing them?

tasks.short: Fill in missing arrival and departure times from paper lists and team lead messages.

today.trigger: Missed clock-ins, broken terminals, or paper shift lists sent in from the sites.
steps: Collect paper lists, photos and Teams messages from team leads
Read and interpret handwritten times
Enter the times in the hours registration
Ask team leads to confirm unclear entries
today.time_sinks: Waiting for team leads to confirm unclear times.

lenses.faster: A model reads photos and messages into draft time lines, and a team lead confirms them in Teams. The specialist only handles disputes, cutting about half the time.
lenses.autonomous: A photo or message in a set Teams channel starts the extraction. The draft goes to the team lead for confirmation before it posts.
lenses.ambitious: A group served for the first time: night shifts get a simple Teams form, so a missed clock-in is fixed the same night instead of waiting until month end. Demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss decoding handwriting. The specialist wants more time fixing why clock-ins fail.
lenses.altitude: The specialist sets the rules for when a manual time is accepted and works with the sites to end paper lists.
reach: Take over hours correction requests now sent to the HR Administrators

tasks.human_edge: Settling disputes where an employee and a team lead remember a shift differently.
tasks.pattern_why: Photos and chat messages are messy input, and one model call turns them into time lines a team lead can check.

in_practice.trigger: A photo or message is posted in the site's hours channel in Teams.
steps: Model extracts names, dates and times
Names are matched to AFAS employee numbers
Draft lines go to the team lead
Team lead confirms
Lines post to AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: The team lead confirms each line before it counts; disputes go to the specialist.
in_practice.logs_to: The Teams thread with the confirmation, and AFAS hours history.

evidence.claim: Reading timesheet documents into structured lines is a typical single model step.

risks: Misread handwriting pays someone for the wrong hours
Manual times invite misuse if confirmation is skipped
research_questions: How many manual time entries are made per month, per site?
How accurate is extraction on a sample of real paper lists?
Would team leads confirm in Teams within a day?

tasks.short: Turn a signed offer and new-hire documents into a complete pay record in AFAS before the first payday.

today.trigger: A candidate signs an offer in Recruitee and HR sends the start details.
steps: Collect the contract, ID copy, bank details and tax credit form
Check that the documents are complete and valid
Enter the employee, contract and pay items in AFAS
Enrol the employee in the pension scheme and set the CAO scale
Chase missing documents by mail
drudgery: Retyping offer data from Recruitee into AFAS
today.time_sinks: Missing documents, and peak season with many hires at once.

lenses.faster: Offer data flows from Recruitee into an AFAS draft, and a model reads the uploaded documents into it and flags gaps. The specialist checks and approves, cutting about half the time.
lenses.autonomous: A signed offer in Recruitee starts the draft record and an automatic request for missing documents. The specialist approves before the first run.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to new hires: a preview of their first payslip in week one, which supports the input metric 'onboarding completed in week one'. Demand would grow in peak season.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss retyping offers. The specialist wants more time helping new people with their pay questions.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the hire-to-pay handover rules agreed with the Recruiters and HR Administrators.
reach: Take over the HR Administrator's contract entry in AFAS; this needs knowledge of the contract templates

tasks.human_edge: Judging unusual cases such as foreign workers, residence permits or the 30% ruling.
tasks.pattern_why: Most data moves by fixed field mapping, and one model call reads scanned documents into fields that are then checked.

in_practice.trigger: An offer is marked signed in Recruitee.
steps: Offer fields map to an AFAS draft
Model reads the ID, bank and tax credit documents
Rules check completeness and validity
Missing items are requested from the new hire
Specialist approves the record
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves the record before the first payroll run.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS employee record history, with the source documents.

evidence.claim: Model reading of personnel documents needs works council consent and care under GDPR.

risks: ID and BSN data handled by a model needs strict AVG controls
A wrong CAO scale set at the start persists for months
research_questions: Is there a working connector or API path from Recruitee to AFAS?
How many hires per month are there in peak season, and how long does each take now?
What share of new-hire records needed a correction later?

tasks.short: Pull hours, production and pay data from all sites into one monthly overview for payroll and finance.

today.trigger: Monthly payroll close and Finance requests for labour cost per site.
steps: Export hours and production data per site
Merge them in Excel
Match them to AFAS pay results
Send overviews to Finance and the site managers
drudgery: Rebuilding the same Excel merge every month
today.time_sinks: Fixing mismatched codes between site exports and AFAS.

lenses.faster: A fixed data pipeline merges site and AFAS data into Power BI, and the specialist checks totals. This cuts about two thirds of the time.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS extract triggers the merge, and mismatches are flagged.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to operations: site managers get labour cost per shift every week. Demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss the Excel merge. The specialist wants more time analysing labour cost.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the payroll data definitions that Finance uses.
reach: Supply the FP&A Analysts with labour cost actuals; this needs the cost centre logic
Check staffing agency invoices against hours with the Bookkeepers

tasks.human_edge: Explaining odd site figures to Finance and managers.
tasks.pattern_why: Merging fixed exports on fixed keys needs no model.

steps: Load the site exports and AFAS data
Map the codes
Flag mismatches
Publish to Power BI
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist signs off the monthly totals before Finance uses them.
in_practice.logs_to: The Power BI refresh log and the mismatch list.

evidence.claim: Merging fixed exports into a nightly-refreshed dashboard is routine BI work that needs no model.

risks: If labour cost per shift is used to score people, it can count as high-risk under the AI Act from 2 December 2027
research_questions: Which site exports change format most often?
Would Finance trust the Power BI totals without the Excel file?
Can agency hours be added from the staffing agency portals?

role.altitude: The specialist stops keying and matching and runs the payroll rule set: CAO allowance and leave rules, pre-run checks and their thresholds, approval of each run, and the pay data for transparency reporting. They gain the right to block a run and to decide which mutations post automatically, and the job gets more expert.
reach: HR Administrator: entering contract changes, exits and new hires in AFAS
Bookkeeper: checking staffing agency invoices against hours
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: preparing pay transparency and gender pay gap data
FP&A Analyst: labour cost actuals per site
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks take about 780 of the role's 1,600 hours a year, and roughly 400 of those hours could go. The limits are AFAS import paths, data quality at the sites, works council consent, and the rule that pay calculation stays deterministic.
skills_to_grow: Writing and testing payroll rules and checks
Handling data under the AVG and basic AI Act duties
role.ambitious_version: Run a first-time-right payroll for office, shift and night staff alike: daily hours checks, a payslip assistant that says it is AI and quotes the calculation, and answers to pay transparency requests within days.
